0.reason: A redundant conjunction; the preceding assertions already pin the phase.

findings.text: tests/test_a_repaired_status_moves_the_run_phase.py:153 asserts `not (live["effective_phase"] == "blocked" and "--role review" in next_action)`, a conjunction whose first operand line 137 and line 138 have already asserted False, so it cannot fail under any code the preceding assertions permit.

tests/test_a_repaired_status_moves_the_run_phase.py:182 asserts `os.environ["RECKON_HOME"] == str(crew_home)`, which restates the fixture's own monkeypatch rather than anything the code under test does, so it is true whatever repair_manifest_status returns.

tests/test_a_repaired_status_moves_the_run_phase.py:158 compares `record["previous_phase"]` against "blocked", the phase the test itself wrote into the fixture pointer at line 79, so an implementation that hardcoded the phase it replaced would satisfy it; it does redden if the read is dropped, because the value would then be None.

reckon/crew/runs.py:2232 rewrites the manifest before reckon/crew/runs.py:2235 writes the pointer, so a failed pointer write leaves the two records disagreeing with the function raising, and the guarantee the docstring states at runs.py:2220 covers only a pointer that cannot be read.

the done-when's importer clause names the test files importing the changed modules but was met over six files chosen by hand, the population of 724 files having been cancelled at about 4 percent, so the importer measure as asserted is not fully satisfied; the deviation is disclosed, and both bounded arms carry the same single pre-existing failure.
